hero.headline: Add Italy to your portfolio. We handle the groundwork.
hero.subhead: You already know how to recruit. What stops most agencies from selling Italy is everything that happens after the student boards the plane — a consulate, a university, a police headquarters, a tax office and a landlord, none of which answer email in your timezone. That is the part we run, on the ground, in Italian.

market.heading: The destination your catalogue is probably missing
market.body: Your competitors are all selling the same four English-speaking destinations, into a market where tuition keeps rising and visa policy keeps tightening. Italy sits in a different price bracket entirely, teaches a growing share of its degrees in English, and runs a means-tested scholarship system that can take a student's tuition to zero. The demand is there. What has been missing is anyone reliable to hand the student to once they land.

model.heading: You own the relationship. We own the ground.
model.body: We work as your destination partner in Italy, not as a competing agency. You run marketing, recruitment and the relationship with the family in your own market — the part you are good at and the part that costs you money to build. Once the student's Universitaly pre-registration opens, the file moves to us and stays with one named coordinator until they are enrolled, permitted and housed. You get the reporting throughout, and the student stays yours.

model.commitmentsHeading: What we put in the agreement, because you will ask
commitments: We do not market to your students, and we do not recruit in your market. Our acquisition happens here or through you.
The student remains your client for the duration of the agreement. We report to you, not around you.
Commercial terms — sub-agency status, commission split, payment triggers — are agreed in writing before the first student is referred, not settled afterwards.
You get a named coordinator with direct contact, not a shared inbox and a ticket number.

advantages.heading: Three failures that come back to you, not to us
advantages.body: When something goes wrong five thousand kilometres away, the family does not call the Italian landlord. They call the agency that sold them the plan. Each of these is a failure your team currently absorbs without having any way to prevent it.

items.title: The lease that does not exist
items.body: Rental fraud against arriving international students is the most common way an Italian placement goes wrong: a deposit wired for a flat that was never available, from a listing that disappears the same week. We view, verify and read the lease line by line before anyone transfers money, and we register it afterwards — which is also what the student's residency depends on.
items.risk: A student who arrives to no address, and a refund conversation you did not cause

items.title: The file the consulate turns away
items.body: Every consulate applies the published requirements its own way, and a file that satisfies one is refused by another. We pre-qualify the student's documents against the standard of the specific consulate that will see them, before the appointment is booked rather than after it is lost.
items.risk: A refusal that costs the student an academic year and costs you the referral

items.title: The margin nobody defined
items.body: Most destination arrangements fall apart on commercial terms that were never written down. We work as a sub-agency partner with a defined commission split, agreed per partner and set out before the first referral. Terms depend on volume and on how much of the route you want us to carry, so we quote them in the conversation rather than publishing a rate card that would fit nobody.
items.risk: An arrangement that pays well on the first cohort and quietly stops working on the fifth

otherPartners.heading: Two more conversations we want to be having
otherPartners.body: Kimere is built to sit between the student and the Italian systems that will not talk to each other. That makes two other kinds of organisation natural counterparts, and we are open to both.

items.title: University international offices
items.body: Incoming international students absorb a volume of individual administrative support your office was never resourced to give — permit filings, fiscal codes, residency, health cover, housing disputes. We handle those individually, off your team's desk, without representing ourselves as the university.
items.looking: A referral route for admitted students who need the administrative side handled

items.title: Student housing operators
items.body: Purpose-built student accommodation solves the single hardest problem an arriving international student has — but the booking, the guarantor requirement and the paperwork are usually where a non-resident applicant falls out of the funnel. We can bring pre-qualified students with their documentation already in order.

howToStart.heading: How a partnership actually starts
howToStart.body: No exclusivity on day one, and no signature before both teams have watched the process run. Four steps, and the first one costs you a call.

steps.title: A first conversation
steps.body: Your current volumes, the destinations you already serve, and whether Italy fits the students you actually recruit. Thirty minutes, and we will tell you if it does not.

steps.title: The boundary, on paper
steps.body: Exactly where your work ends and ours begins, what we report and when, and the commercial terms in writing. Nothing about the split is left to be worked out later.

steps.title: A small first cohort
steps.body: A handful of students, run end to end, so both teams see the process work on real files with real deadlines before anyone commits to volume.

steps.title: A formal agreement
steps.body: Signed once the pilot has confirmed the model fits — with terms based on what the first cohort actually showed, not on what either side projected.

dueDiligence.heading: Due diligence, in advance
items: Kimere began operating in June 2026 and the legal structure is being formalised. We will share current company documentation directly at the due-diligence stage rather than describe it here.

We hold no formal agreement with, and no accreditation from, any Italian university or public body. Where a page of this site describes what a university or a consulate does, it links that institution's own published source.

We do not issue visas or residence permits and we do not guarantee outcomes. Those decisions belong to the consulate and the Questura, and any partner promising you otherwise is selling something they cannot deliver.
We are not a licensed estate agency. We view, verify and register housing; we do not hold listings or take deposits on anyone's behalf.

form.heading: Tell us what you send, and where
form.body: This form goes to the person who would run the partnership, not to a sales queue. Give us the volumes and the markets and we will come back with a straight answer on whether the model fits — including if it does not.
